[DataSquad logged {{< var datasquad.tasks_2025 >}} reportable project tasks in 2025.]{.lede}

DataSquad is DSC's peer-consulting model: undergraduate and graduate student
consultants providing sustained project support alongside DSC staff's direct
consultations. It logged **{{< var datasquad.tasks_2025 >}} reportable project tasks in 2025**,
much of it sustained, hands-on project support rather than one-off questions. Task
tracking in Trello began in 2023, so the rise from {{< var datasquad.tasks_2023 >}} tasks
that year partly reflects record-keeping, not only more work.

The program started in 2020 on a gift from **Norman Powell**, which funded student
salaries and laptops for the first cohort. The Library added funding in 2023 to
expand the team and add in-person hours. In 2024, DataSquad absorbed the LuxLab
student program after its funding source, CLICC funds, became restricted, merging two
student-support lines into one.

It's also a verified career pipeline, not just a service to faculty: all
{{< var datasquad.placement_n >}} identified graduates of the {{< var datasquad.placement_cohort >}}
cohort found placements, at employers including {{< var datasquad.placement_names >}}. Several of the same students worked
on DataSquad's highest-profile faculty projects before landing those placements.
Lawrence Lee, credited above for the Carceral Ecologies speedup, is now a Software
Development Engineer at Amazon.
